source.branch_note: The branch name is informational only. `git ls-remote` shows openwrt-21.02 as the single branch and as HEAD, but the build never resolves a branch: it checks out the full 40 character commit above, so a moving branch cannot change the build input.

source.selection_evidence: git ls-remote of the repository returns exactly one ref, refs/heads/openwrt-21.02, equal to the revision above. A blob filtered clone of that commit confirms target/linux/mediatek/Makefile KERNEL_PATCHVER:=5.4, target/linux/mediatek/mt7981/target.mk (ARCH aarch64, SUBTARGET mt7981), existing NX30 Pro board support in image/mt7981.mk (Device/h3c_nx30pro, IMAGE_SIZE 65536k), files-5.4/arch/arm64/boot/dts/mediatek/mt7981-h3c-nx30pro.dts with the generic,nmbm binding over lower-mtd-device = <&spi_nand>, and mt7981/base-files/etc/board.d/{01_leds,02_network} plus lib/upgrade/platform.sh (nand_do_upgrade). This base carries the board support the requirement asks to keep, unlike a general ImmortalWrt tree.

rejected_sources.reason: This was the active base of the earlier lock and of the repeatedly failing firmware Action. It is the same tree as the Galaxian port below: `git ls-remote` of hanwckf/immortalwrt-mt798x lists refs/pull/135/head = 78cf22edddf07443d8f0506c9f361d3498475189, i.e. the commit is an unmerged pull request, not a maintained branch. Its pinned feed commits (packages c494d5269421c94090b56a971b9796c21f808a55, luci 97b019be0a676c48ec2d804f0aace49cefcbb365) are not the heads of the frozen openwrt-21.02 feed branches, which is why the last `make defconfig` dropped PassWall, Xray, cloudflared, DDNS, ZeroTier, Docker and Argon. It must never be the active source; it stays readable only as failure evidence.

port_reference.detail: The 2023 tree that defines Device/h3c_nx30pro_112M in target/linux/mediatek/image/mt7981.mk and mt7981-h3c-nx30pro-112M.dts. Its five partitions (BL2 0x0/0x100000, u-boot-env 0x100000/0x80000, Factory 0x180000/0x200000, FIP 0x380000/0x200000, ubi 0x580000/0x7000000) are byte for byte the immortalwrt-112m table the boot loader lock carries. The device port is derived from it in Task 2 and rebased onto the hanwckf commit above; the 2023 commit itself is never built.

build_readiness.required_evidence: An authorized disposable Linux or Actions run that installs the four locked feeds, runs `make defconfig` for mediatek/mt7981 with devices/nx30pro/config.config and proves every hard gate symbol is still =y in the final .config.
build_readiness.gate_note: firmware_lock.py check recomputes this flag from the package table. Hand setting ready=true while a hard gate is unproven is itself an error, so the flag cannot be flipped without the evidence.
build_readiness.promotion_note: manifests/sources.json stays at revision UNRESOLVED while ready=false, which keeps tools/manifest.py resolve --require-build-ready and scripts/build.sh stopped at the repository build-not-ready status 3. It is set equal to source.revision only after the probe above passed.

target.evidence: A recursive search for 'nx30' under target/linux/mediatek of the pinned commit returns only the five stock files (image/mt7981.mk Device/h3c_nx30pro with IMAGE_SIZE 65536k, files-5.4/.../mt7981-h3c-nx30pro.dts, mt7981/base-files/etc/board.d/01_leds, 02_network, lib/upgrade/platform.sh). There is no 112M profile and no 112M device tree upstream, so both are ported from the Galaxian reference by devices/nx30pro/patches and stay unverified until Task 2 checks them against this lock. The stock tree also has no mt7981-h3c-nx30pro-base.dtsi, which the reference 112M device tree includes; the port must add it or inline the shared nodes.

image.image_size_note: IMAGE_SIZE := 110592k is the upper bound of the factory image, taken from the 112M port reference, not a measured size. The UBI partition of the partition contract is 112 MiB, so the image has about 4 MiB of head room. Both stay UNRESOLVED until the first real build reports them.
image.verification_note: These rules are read from the Galaxian 112M port reference, not from the pinned source. Task 2 verifies them against the ported profile.

partition_contract.source: devices/nx30pro/uboot/uboot-source-lock.json layouts.entries["immortalwrt-112m"], which is the /mtd-layout/layout@1 node of the pinned boot loader device tree
partition_contract.address_space_note: All offsets are addresses inside the NMBM logical device nmbm0 that the boot loader and the system expose. They are never physical NAND addresses.
partition_contract.label_note: The system device tree spells BL2 and FIP in upper case, the boot loader mtdparts string spells them bl2 and fip. Only the case differs; the offsets and sizes are identical and the contract tests compare them case insensitively.

package_contract_note: Every entry names the exact OpenWrt config symbols, the feed that provides it, the full commit of that feed, the provider path read at that commit, and a status. `candidate` means the package was read from the feed index at the pinned commit but no `make defconfig` proved it survives configuration; nothing may be marked `available` without that evidence. `dependency_closure_scope` below states how far the static dependency enumeration reaches.
dependency_closure_scope: Direct DEPENDS/LUCI_DEPENDS entries are enumerated in `dependencies` only for the packages whose closure was read completely at the pinned commits: luci-app-passwall, dockerd and luci-ssl-openssl. These are the packages the old Action dropped, so their closure is the one that has to be checkable statically. For the remaining entries `dependencies` is empty and only the provider path is verified; their transitive closure is exactly what the authorized `make defconfig` probe has to prove, and until then every one of them stays `candidate`.

packages.detail: The earlier lock claimed this 5.4 base carries no WireGuard module. That claim is wrong and is corrected here: the pinned hanwckf tree ships target/linux/generic/backport-5.4/080-wireguard-* backport patches, defines KernelPackage/wireguard (drivers/net/wireguard/wireguard.ko) in package/kernel/linux/modules/netsupport.mk and carries wireguard-tools 1.0.20210914. What is not proven is that it builds and runs on mediatek/mt7981: target/linux/generic/config-5.4 ships `# CONFIG_WIREGUARD is not set`, so the module is not enabled by default and no defconfig evidence exists. The requirement therefore stays UNRESOLVED instead of being recorded as either available or impossible.

sing-box does not exist in the packages feed at the pinned commit, and luci-app-sing-box does not exist in the luci feed. Modern releases need a Go toolchain generation this 21.02 base does not provide, and PassWall 4.68 offers the Xray backend only. The approved design does not require sing-box and explicitly excludes it together with HomeProxy, OpenClash, PassWall2 and AdGuard Home, so the transparent proxy requirement is met with Xray and the difference is recorded here instead of shipping a second proxy manager.

system_dependencies.source: target/linux/mediatek/mt7981/base-files/etc/board.d/02_network at the pinned source commit, case h3c,nx30pro
system_dependencies.detail: The base reads the WAN MAC with mtd_get_mac_ascii ethaddr from the pdt_data_1 partition and derives the LAN MAC from it.
system_dependencies.impact: The 112M partition contract has no pdt_data_1 partition, so the stock source of the MAC does not exist on this layout. The device patch takes the MAC from a provisioned file, then from the factory data area, and only then from the stock partition when it is still there.
system_dependencies.status: handled by devices/nx30pro/patches/0001-mediatek-nx30pro-wan-mac-source.patch, verified against the pinned source in Task 2

system_dependencies.source: target/linux/mediatek/mt7981/base-files/etc/board.d/02_network at the pinned source commit, case h3c,nx30pro
system_dependencies.detail: When mtk_factory_get_byte "Factory" 4 2 returns 00-0c, the base writes a MAC derived from the WAN MAC into the Factory partition at offset 4 with mtk_facrory_write_mac.
system_dependencies.impact: The first boot can modify the factory data area, so the area has to be backed up before the system is started. The patch keeps this behaviour but only when a real WAN MAC was found.
system_dependencies.status: handled by devices/nx30pro/patches/0001-mediatek-nx30pro-wan-mac-source.patch, verified against the pinned source in Task 2
